name: Xtglobal Infotech Ltd
title: Xtglobal Infotech Ltd - 531225 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Soft IT-services quarter: consolidated revenue +1.1% YoY to ₹93.30 cr, with EBITDA margin up to 7.6% on offshoring mix shift; no supply-side or capex content, and US public-sector and Ireland entry are early-stage.

triggers.quote: the margin moving to 7.6% from 4.8% in Q4 2026 and 7.1% in Q1 2026

Revenue figures appear inconsistent (₹719.19 cr standalone vs ₹93.30 cr consolidated)

summary.headline: Xtglobal Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 7.6% from 4.8% in Q4 FY26, while consolidated revenue grew only 1.1% YoY to ₹93.30 crore.
summary.overview: Management described a steady quarter with a cautious IT services demand environment and a shift from onsite to offshore delivery. Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹719.19 crore and standalone PAT rose 19.8% YoY to ₹1.82 crore. Consolidated revenue was ₹93.30 crore (+1.1% YoY, +2% QoQ), with consolidated EBITDA of ₹7.06 crore and PAT of ₹3.89 crore (+4.3% YoY). The company added seven FinAcc engagements across Australia, the US and Ireland, and entered Ireland with its first FinAcc outsourcing client.

financial_highlights.change: +76.3% YoY; margin +571 bps YoY (vs 9% in Q1 FY26)
+1.1% YoY vs ₹92.31 crore; +2% QoQ vs ₹89.52 crore
+7.8% YoY; margin up from 4.8% in Q4 FY26 and 7.1% in Q1 FY26; +64.2% QoQ

segments.name: Product (AP / Circulus automation)
segments.commentary: Management cited a ~25% margin on the product business, which it said is about 25% of total revenue; AP SaaS product is 15-20% of revenue. Circulus is positioned as a sticky, long-term automation product.

segments.name: Finance & Accounting services
segments.commentary: Around 14% of revenue, described as recurring; clients typically start with AP and add AR and R2R, with one client scaling from one resource to 10.

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Added clients in India and the US during the quarter; no revenue or margin figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Australia and Ireland focus to grow next year, targeting roughly US$1 million in each local currency over the next year (as stated).
International revenue is currently under 10% of total, expected to stay at that level for the next couple of years.
Management said offshore shift will keep margins higher even though revenue per resource is roughly halved; cited as sustainable.
Dividend: management said it is considering one this financial year, likely next quarter after results.
Zoho internal implementation is 90% complete across ~13 products/modules; stabilisation is the remaining goal.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were disclosed in the call.

Commissioning timelines: none stated. Zoho implementation (ERP/paperless internal transformation) reported 90% complete across around 13 products and modules in Q1 FY27; the remaining goal is stabilisation and realising expected operational benefits.

Delivery footprint: offshore delivery from India delivery centres; the first Irish FinAcc engagement will be run from India. Management said the US mix will rise as public-sector work is delivered onshore, versus mostly offshore delivery over the past three years.
Management referenced a targeted expansion in Australia and Ireland/Europe to about US$1 million each in local currency over the next year, with no capacity or capex detail given.
demand_pricing: Industry demand described as cautious: clients selective on discretionary spend and decision cycles longer.
AI moving from experimentation to practical enterprise deployment, creating both pressure and opportunity.
Won general empanelment in a couple of US government contracts; specific RFPs still to be won, public sector a new focus area.
GCC strategy targets US mid-market customers starting with 3-5 member teams that can scale to ~50.
Consolidated revenue growth of 1.1% YoY attributed by management to onsite-to-offshore shift, which lowers per-resource billing (e.g., $70 onsite vs $35 offshore).

qa_highlights.question: How does management see PaaS evolving as a growth engine, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on Australia and Ireland/Europe; management expects these to reach about US$1 million each in local currency over the next year. International is under 10% of revenue today.

qa_highlights.question: Which areas (AI, cloud, automation, digital transformation) offer growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees most growth in AI and cloud; the company has won general empanelment in a couple of US government contracts, with individual RFPs still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to deepen wallet share with existing global clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing US clients were the main revenue base until last year; AP SaaS is 15-20% of revenue and grows with client volumes. One new client was added and incremental work is being sold to existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: How to build scale in US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue to rise via public sector and onshore delivery, versus mostly offshore delivery over the past three years. Europe started with the first Irish client.

qa_highlights.question: How is GCC engagement building into larger relationships?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting mid-market GCC customers that start with 3-5 people and can grow to about 50 members, mainly in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated revenue up only 1.1% YoY and how sustainable is 7.6% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slow growth to onsite-to-offshore shift (same work at roughly half the cost) and said margin gains are sustainable because expenses fell sharply and offshore margins are higher.

qa_highlights.question: Which services have the highest margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Product (about 25% margin, about 25% of revenue) and F&A (about 14% of revenue) were cited as recurring, high-margin lines.

risks_watch: Consolidated revenue growth of only 1.1% YoY despite the 7.6% EBITDA margin; check whether revenue recovers as offshore mix shifts.
Standalone and consolidated figures differ sharply (standalone revenue ₹719 crore vs consolidated ₹93 crore); the basis of the standalone numbers needs clarification.
Management's statement that standalone PAT was ₹1.82 crore with 9.5% margin conflicts with the 9.5% margin on ₹719 crore revenue; verify the stated figures.
Public-sector and US government revenue is at the empanelment stage with no RFP wins yet quantified.
Dividend decision deferred to next quarter; no commitment made.
Zoho ERP/paperless migration at 90% completion; stabilisation risk remains.
summary.management_tone: Measured and somewhat qualitative: management was confident on margin gains and client wins, but gave few hard numbers on order book, pricing or US revenue targets. Answers on revenue growth and dividend were loosely framed and deferred.
key_quotes: Yes, that number is true, actually. Because the expense is also drastically reduced.
The product, we have a 25% margin, 25% out of our total revenue, 25% is product, and around 14% is coming from finance and accounting services.
So, this year we think about, but next quarter maybe we will consider, once we declare the results, right?

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management targets roughly US$1 million each in Australia and Ireland over the next year with no capacity or capex detail, and consolidated revenue grew only 1.1% YoY on the onsite-to-offshore shift, so growth backing is vague.
